bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/social.rs (service request assembly), springboard/sdk/src/multipart.rs (multipart body), springboard/ui/src/compose.rs (post draft model), springboard/sdk/src/share.rs (share sheet to installed apps), springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (URLRequest, URLSession); no social-network service
summary: BifrOSt now has the post draft model, the request assembly with parameters and multipart uploads, and the multipart body builder. It has no compose sheet that shows or posts to a network, no service types, and no signed-in social account store.

features.note: The draft model holds the post content and dismissal result. No shell sheet shows it, and the share menu does not post to a network.
No service types exist to check.

features.apple: setInitialText(_:), add(_:) for images and URLs, removeAllImages(), removeAllURLs()
features.note: The content API matches the framework. Nothing in the shell edits a draft yet, and the limit of 8 images and 8 links is BifrOSt's own (the framework states none).

features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/compose.rs (ComposeResult::Done, Cancelled, ComposeDraft::dismiss); springboard/sdk/src/share.rs (App::share_done via show_picker)
features.note: The result values match the framework. The share menu still reports the chosen app id, not the compose result.

features.feature: HTTP request assembly for a service
features.note: Methods GET, POST, DELETE and PUT, query strings, form bodies and multipart bodies are assembled. There is no service type, and perform goes through URLSession rather than a request object.
Named file parts with optional file name and type, and text fields. The boundary is kept out of the part data. Covered by unit tests.
No account store and no OAuth or token signing. BifrOSt Cloud accounts live in ~/Projects/bifrost-cloud, outside this repo.

features.feature: Receiving shared content in an extension
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/share.rs (manifest handles and schemes; Input::Open; App::document)
features.note: An app can receive shared URLs, text and files. There is no separate extension process.
Named third-party networks, several of them defunct. Tied to Apple's service list, not to a desktop capability.

gaps: No compose sheet that shows the draft and posts it to a network (the draft model in springboard/ui/src/compose.rs has no UI or transport).
No social account store or request signing (SLRequest.account equivalent).
No service types and no service availability check (isAvailable(forServiceType:) equivalent).
The share menu offers only installed apps, with no per-item NSSharingService objects or delegate callbacks (see docs/bifrost-ui.md, 'Share sheet' gaps).
The compose result is not wired to the share menu's completion (App::share_done reports an app id, not Done or Cancelled).
